WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT
        DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at) AS month,
        SUM(amount) AS total
    FROM payments
    WHERE status = 'completed'
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at)

FROM monthly

title: window functions with partition

    e.department,
    e.salary,
    RANK() OVER (
        PARTITION BY e.department
        ORDER BY e.salary DESC

title: multi-cte with left join
code:
WITH active_users AS (
    SELECT id, name, email
    FROM users
    WHERE active = true
),
recent_orders AS (
    SELECT user_id,
        COUNT(*) AS order_count,
        MAX(created_at) AS last_order
    FROM orders
    WHERE created_at >= CURRENT_DATE
        - INTERVAL '90 days'
    GROUP BY user_id
)
SELECT a.name, a.email,
    COALESCE(r.order_count, 0) AS orders_90d,
    r.last_order
FROM active_users a
LEFT JOIN recent_orders r
    ON r.user_id = a.id
ORDER BY orders_90d DESC;
notes: Chains two CTEs to join active users with their recent 90-day order activity.

    updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
FROM (

    FROM order_items
    WHERE order_id IN (
            SELECT id FROM orders
            WHERE status = 'confirmed'
                AND created_at >= CURRENT_DATE

) o
WHERE i.product_id = o.product_id

notes: Decrements inventory based on confirmed order totals from a nested derived table.

title: upsert with on conflict
code:
INSERT INTO product_stats (
    product_id, view_count, last_viewed_at
)
SELECT
    pv.product_id,
    COUNT(*) AS views,
    MAX(pv.viewed_at) AS last_view
FROM page_views pv
WHERE pv.viewed_at >= CURRENT_DATE
    - INTERVAL '1 day'
GROUP BY pv.product_id
ON CONFLICT (product_id)
DO UPDATE SET
    view_count = product_stats.view_count
        + EXCLUDED.view_count,
    last_viewed_at = GREATEST(
        product_stats.last_viewed_at,
        EXCLUDED.last_viewed_at
    );
notes: Aggregates daily page views and upserts into stats, accumulating counts and keeping the latest timestamp.

title: window lag with trend classification
code:
WITH daily_rev AS (
    SELECT
        DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at) AS day,
        SUM(amount) AS revenue
    FROM payments
    WHERE status = 'completed'
        AND created_at >= CURRENT_DATE
            - INTERVAL '60 days'
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)
)
SELECT
    day,
    revenue,
    LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY day) AS prev_day,
    CASE
        WHEN LAG(revenue) OVER (
                ORDER BY day
            ) IS NULL THEN 'N/A'
        WHEN revenue > LAG(revenue) OVER (
                ORDER BY day
            ) * 1.10 THEN 'growth'
        WHEN revenue < LAG(revenue) OVER (
                ORDER BY day
            ) * 0.90 THEN 'decline'
        ELSE 'stable'
    END AS trend
FROM daily_rev
ORDER BY day;
notes: Classifies daily revenue trends by comparing each day to the prior using LAG inside a CASE expression.

title: lateral join with date series
code:
SELECT
    d.day::DATE,
    COALESCE(s.total_sales, 0.00) AS total_sales,
    COALESCE(s.order_count, 0) AS order_count
FROM GENERATE_SERIES(
        CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days',
        CURRENT_DATE,
        '1 day'::INTERVAL
    ) AS d(day)
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT
            SUM(o.total) AS total_sales,
            COUNT(*) AS order_count
        FROM orders o
        WHERE o.created_at >= d.day
            AND o.created_at < d.day
                + INTERVAL '1 day'
            AND o.status IN (
                'shipped', 'delivered'
            )
    ) s ON true
ORDER BY d.day;
notes: Generates a continuous date range and lateral joins daily order totals, filling gaps with zeros.

title: percentile analytics with ntile
code:
WITH scored AS (
    SELECT
        e.id,
        e.name,
        e.department,
        e.salary,
        NTILE(4) OVER (
            PARTITION BY e.department
            ORDER BY e.salary
        ) AS quartile,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY e.department
            ORDER BY e.salary
        ) AS pct_rank
    FROM employees e
    WHERE e.active = true
)
SELECT
    name,
    department,
    salary,
    quartile,
    ROUND(pct_rank::NUMERIC, 3) AS pct_rank
FROM scored
WHERE quartile = 4
ORDER BY department, salary DESC;
notes: Assigns salary quartiles and percent ranks within departments, filtering for top quartile employees.

title: writeable cte upsert pattern
code:
WITH incoming AS (
    SELECT
        sku,
        SUM(quantity) AS total_qty,
        MAX(received_at) AS last_recv
    FROM shipment_items
    WHERE shipment_id IN (
            SELECT id FROM shipments
            WHERE status = 'arrived'
                AND processed = false
        )
    GROUP BY sku
),
updated AS (
    UPDATE warehouse_stock ws
    SET on_hand = ws.on_hand + i.total_qty,
        last_restock = i.last_recv
    FROM incoming i
    WHERE ws.sku = i.sku
    RETURNING ws.sku
)
INSERT INTO warehouse_stock (
    sku, on_hand, last_restock
)
SELECT sku, total_qty, last_recv
FROM incoming
WHERE sku NOT IN (
        SELECT sku FROM updated
    );
notes: Uses writeable CTEs to update existing stock and insert new SKUs from arrived shipments.

title: grouping sets with filter clause

SELECT
    COALESCE(region, '(all)') AS region,
    COALESCE(category, '(all)') AS category,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(total) AS revenue,
    ROUND(AVG(total), 2) AS avg_order,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE total >= 100.00
        ) AS large_orders
FROM orders o
JOIN products p
    ON p.id = o.product_id
WHERE o.created_at >= '2024-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (
        (region, category),
        (region),
        (category),
        ()
    )
ORDER BY region NULLS LAST,
    category NULLS LAST;
notes: Produces subtotals by region, category, combinations, and grand total using GROUPING SETS.

title: recursive cte for org hierarchy
code:
WITH RECURSIVE org_tree AS (
    SELECT
        id,
        name,
        manager_id,
        1 AS depth,
        ARRAY[name] AS path
    FROM employees
    WHERE manager_id IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        e.id,
        e.name,
        e.manager_id,
        t.depth + 1,
        t.path || e.name
    FROM employees e
    INNER JOIN org_tree t
        ON t.id = e.manager_id
    WHERE t.depth < 10
)
SELECT
    id,
    name,
    depth,
    ARRAY_TO_STRING(path, ' > ') AS chain,
    REPEAT('  ', depth - 1) || name AS indented
FROM org_tree
ORDER BY path;
notes: Traverses an employee hierarchy recursively, building breadcrumb paths from root to each node.

title: monthly sales pivot with trend
code:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', sold_at) AS month,
        SUM(quantity) AS qty,
        SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue
    FROM sales
    WHERE sold_at >= DATE_TRUNC('year',
            CURRENT_DATE)
    GROUP BY product_id,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', sold_at)
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        m.*,
        p.name AS product_name,
        p.category,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY m.month
            ORDER BY m.revenue DESC
        ) AS month_rank,
        LAG(m.revenue) OVER (
            PARTITION BY m.product_id
            ORDER BY m.month
        ) AS prev_revenue
    FROM monthly m
    JOIN products p ON p.id = m.product_id
)
SELECT
    product_name,
    category,
    month,
    revenue,
    month_rank,
    CASE
        WHEN prev_revenue IS NULL THEN 'new'
        WHEN revenue > prev_revenue * 1.20
            THEN 'surge'
        WHEN revenue < prev_revenue * 0.80
            THEN 'drop'
        ELSE 'steady'
    END AS trend
FROM ranked
WHERE month_rank <= 5
ORDER BY month, month_rank;
notes: Ranks monthly product sales and classifies revenue trends compared to prior months.

title: plpgsql function for date bucketing
code:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION date_bucket_summary(
    p_start DATE,
    p_end DATE,
    p_interval INTERVAL DEFAULT '1 week'
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    bucket_start DATE,
    bucket_end DATE,
    order_count BIGINT,
    total_revenue NUMERIC(12, 2),
    avg_order NUMERIC(10, 2)
) AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        d.day::DATE AS bucket_start,
        (d.day + p_interval)::DATE
            AS bucket_end,
        COUNT(o.id) AS order_count,
        COALESCE(SUM(o.total), 0.00)
            ::NUMERIC(12, 2),
        COALESCE(AVG(o.total), 0.00)
            ::NUMERIC(10, 2)
    FROM GENERATE_SERIES(
            p_start, p_end, p_interval
        ) AS d(day)
    LEFT JOIN orders o
        ON o.created_at >= d.day
            AND o.created_at < d.day
                + p_interval
    GROUP BY d.day
    ORDER BY d.day;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
notes: Creates a PL/pgSQL function that buckets orders into configurable intervals returning summary stats.

title: materialized view with multi-cte
code:
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_customer_360 AS
WITH order_stats AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
        SUM(total) AS lifetime_value,
        AVG(total) AS avg_order,
        MAX(created_at) AS last_order_at
    FROM orders
    WHERE status IN ('shipped', 'delivered')
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
support_stats AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
        AVG(
            EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM
                resolved_at - created_at
            ) / 3600.0
        ) AS avg_resolution_hrs
    FROM support_tickets
    WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT
    c.id,
    c.name,
    c.email,
    COALESCE(o.total_orders, 0) AS total_orders,
    COALESCE(o.lifetime_value, 0.00)
        AS lifetime_value,
    ROUND(COALESCE(o.avg_order, 0.00), 2)
        AS avg_order,
    o.last_order_at,
    COALESCE(s.ticket_count, 0) AS ticket_count,
    ROUND(
        COALESCE(s.avg_resolution_hrs, 0.0)
            ::NUMERIC, 1
    ) AS avg_resolution_hrs
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN order_stats o
    ON o.customer_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN support_stats s
    ON s.customer_id = c.id;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_mv_cust360_id
    ON mv_customer_360 (id);
notes: Creates a materialized customer 360 view combining order and support metrics with a unique index.

title: json aggregation with correlated subquery
code:
SELECT
    d.name AS department,
    JSON_AGG(
        JSON_BUILD_OBJECT(
            'id', e.id,
            'name', e.name,
            'role', e.role,
            'salary', e.salary,
            'skills', (
                SELECT JSON_AGG(
                        s.name ORDER BY s.name
                    )
                FROM employee_skills es
                JOIN skills s
                    ON s.id = es.skill_id
                WHERE es.employee_id = e.id
            )
        ) ORDER BY e.name
    ) AS members,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount,
    ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary,
    SUM(
        CASE WHEN e.hire_date >= CURRENT_DATE
                - INTERVAL '1 year'
            THEN 1 ELSE 0
        END
    ) AS new_hires
FROM departments d
JOIN employees e
    ON e.department_id = d.id
WHERE d.active = true
GROUP BY d.id, d.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY d.name;
notes: Aggregates employees into nested JSON per department including skills from a correlated subquery.

title: recursive graph with cycle detection
code:
WITH RECURSIVE dep_graph AS (
    SELECT
        s.id AS service_id,
        s.name AS service_name,
        d.depends_on_id,
        1 AS depth,
        ARRAY[s.id] AS visited,
        false AS is_cycle
    FROM services s
    JOIN service_deps d
        ON d.service_id = s.id
    WHERE s.name = 'api-gateway'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        dg.service_id,
        dg.service_name,
        d2.depends_on_id,
        dg.depth + 1,
        dg.visited || d2.service_id,
        d2.depends_on_id = ANY(dg.visited)
    FROM dep_graph dg
    JOIN service_deps d2
        ON d2.service_id = dg.depends_on_id
    WHERE NOT dg.is_cycle
        AND dg.depth < 20
)
SELECT DISTINCT
    service_name,
    dep.name AS dependency,
    g.depth,
    g.is_cycle,
    ARRAY_TO_STRING(
        ARRAY(
            SELECT s2.name
            FROM UNNEST(g.visited)
                WITH ORDINALITY
                AS u(sid, ord)
            JOIN services s2
                ON s2.id = u.sid
            ORDER BY u.ord
        ), ' -> '
    ) AS chain
FROM dep_graph g
JOIN services dep
    ON dep.id = g.depends_on_id
ORDER BY g.depth, dependency;
notes: Recursively walks a service dependency graph detecting cycles and building named traversal chains.

title: conversion funnel with chained ctes
code:
WITH funnel_events AS (
    SELECT
        user_id,
        event_type,
        created_at,
        session_id,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY user_id,
                event_type
            ORDER BY created_at
        ) AS event_seq
    FROM analytics_events
    WHERE event_type IN (
            'page_view', 'add_to_cart',
            'checkout_start', 'purchase'
        )
        AND created_at >= CURRENT_DATE
            - INTERVAL '30 days'
),
first_events AS (
    SELECT user_id, event_type,
        created_at, session_id
    FROM funnel_events
    WHERE event_seq = 1
),
funnel AS (
    SELECT
        pv.user_id,
        pv.created_at AS viewed_at,
        ac.created_at AS carted_at,
        cs.created_at AS checkout_at,
        pu.created_at AS purchased_at,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM
            pu.created_at - pv.created_at
        ) / 3600.0 AS hrs_to_convert
    FROM first_events pv
    LEFT JOIN first_events ac
        ON ac.user_id = pv.user_id
            AND ac.event_type
                = 'add_to_cart'
    LEFT JOIN first_events cs
        ON cs.user_id = pv.user_id
            AND cs.event_type
                = 'checkout_start'
    LEFT JOIN first_events pu
        ON pu.user_id = pv.user_id
            AND pu.event_type
                = 'purchase'
    WHERE pv.event_type = 'page_view'
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_viewers,
    COUNT(carted_at) AS added_to_cart,
    COUNT(checkout_at) AS started_checkout,
    COUNT(purchased_at) AS purchased,
    ROUND(
        100.0 * COUNT(purchased_at)
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2
    ) AS conversion_pct,
    ROUND(
        AVG(hrs_to_convert)::NUMERIC, 1
    ) AS avg_hrs_to_buy
FROM funnel;
notes: Builds a four-step conversion funnel from analytics events using chained CTEs with window deduplication.

title: crosstab pivot with case aggregates
code:
WITH months AS (
    SELECT GENERATE_SERIES(
        DATE_TRUNC('month', CURRENT_DATE)
            - INTERVAL '5 months',
        DATE_TRUNC('month', CURRENT_DATE),
        '1 month'::INTERVAL
    ) AS month_start
),
monthly_sales AS (
    SELECT
        p.category,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', s.sold_at) AS m,
        SUM(s.quantity * s.unit_price)
            AS revenue
    FROM sales s
    JOIN products p
        ON p.id = s.product_id
    WHERE s.sold_at >= (
            SELECT MIN(month_start)
            FROM months
        )
    GROUP BY p.category,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', s.sold_at)
),
pivoted AS (
    SELECT
        ms.category,
        SUM(CASE WHEN ms.m = m0.month_start
            THEN ms.revenue ELSE 0 END)
            AS m0_rev,
        SUM(CASE WHEN ms.m = m1.month_start
            THEN ms.revenue ELSE 0 END)
            AS m1_rev,
        SUM(CASE WHEN ms.m = m2.month_start
            THEN ms.revenue ELSE 0 END)
            AS m2_rev,
        SUM(CASE WHEN ms.m = m3.month_start
            THEN ms.revenue ELSE 0 END)
            AS m3_rev,
        SUM(CASE WHEN ms.m = m4.month_start
            THEN ms.revenue ELSE 0 END)
            AS m4_rev,
        SUM(CASE WHEN ms.m = m5.month_start
            THEN ms.revenue ELSE 0 END)
            AS m5_rev
    FROM monthly_sales ms
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT month_start FROM months
                    OFFSET 0 LIMIT 1) m0
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT month_start FROM months
                    OFFSET 1 LIMIT 1) m1
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT month_start FROM months
                    OFFSET 2 LIMIT 1) m2
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT month_start FROM months
                    OFFSET 3 LIMIT 1) m3
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT month_start FROM months
                    OFFSET 4 LIMIT 1) m4
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT month_start FROM months
                    OFFSET 5 LIMIT 1) m5
    GROUP BY ms.category
)
SELECT
    category,
    m0_rev, m1_rev, m2_rev,
    m3_rev, m4_rev, m5_rev,
    (m0_rev + m1_rev + m2_rev
        + m3_rev + m4_rev + m5_rev)
        AS total
FROM pivoted
ORDER BY total DESC;
notes: Emulates a crosstab by pivoting six months of category revenue using CASE inside aggregates over cross-joined anchors.

title: recursive bom with cost rollup
code:
WITH RECURSIVE bom_tree AS (
    SELECT
        p.id AS part_id,
        p.name AS part_name,
        p.unit_cost,
        1 AS quantity,
        p.unit_cost AS line_cost,
        0 AS depth,
        ARRAY[p.name] AS path
    FROM parts p
    WHERE p.id = 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        child.id,
        child.name,
        child.unit_cost,
        b.qty_required * t.quantity,
        child.unit_cost
            * b.qty_required
            * t.quantity,
        t.depth + 1,
        t.path || child.name
    FROM bom_tree t
    JOIN bill_of_materials b
        ON b.parent_part_id = t.part_id
    JOIN parts child
        ON child.id = b.child_part_id
    WHERE t.depth < 15
        AND NOT (
            child.id = ANY((
                SELECT UNNEST(
                    ARRAY(
                        SELECT p2.id
                        FROM UNNEST(t.path)
                            AS pn
                        JOIN parts p2
                            ON p2.name = pn
                    )
                )
            ))
        )
),
rollup AS (
    SELECT
        part_id,
        part_name,
        depth,
        quantity,
        line_cost,
        SUM(line_cost) OVER ()
            AS total_cost,
        ROUND(
            100.0 * line_cost
                / NULLIF(
                    SUM(line_cost)
                        OVER (), 0
                ), 2
        ) AS cost_pct,
        ARRAY_TO_STRING(
            path, ' / '
        ) AS chain
    FROM bom_tree
)
SELECT
    part_name,
    depth,
    quantity,
    line_cost,
    cost_pct,
    chain
FROM rollup
ORDER BY path;
notes: Explodes a recursive bill of materials with cycle prevention and computes each component cost share of the total.
